attested.reason: The DLMF page defines the continued fraction and its coefficients and prints no worked numerical value of the function, so no printed value is available to check this rule. The one printed value G6 can be run on is in Barber, and the separate barber_example rule carries it.
observations() either returns the observations as floats or raises an MLError; it does not alter values. The shared row check likewise only raises.

The paper's examples are plots of simulated chains whose draws are not printed, and it has no table of diagnostic values from published data. It does print a few values for an eight-schools run (page 25), but they come from a sampler's draws that the paper does not print, so G6's functions cannot be run on them and no printed value checks this rule.

Example 12.2 prints the evidence for 5 heads and 2 tails and for 50 heads and 20 tails, but the fair-coin prior parameters appear in the text about 3,200 characters earlier, with equations and a figure between them, so no single quote of at most 1,500 characters holds the inputs and the printed value together. The cases are transcribed with printed set to false.
The held page gives the fraction and no numerical value to run the function on, and the series page is not held, so no printed value checks this rule.

Algorithm 27.3 and its text print no numerical output that G6's seeded sampler could be run on; its examples are plots of random draws. Only identities (a unit ratio accepts) can be checked, and those are printed: false.

check() computes the predictive interval and returns descriptive numbers beside the misfit flag; it changes no posterior and no label, and its only other effects are the refusals the rule lists plus a refusal for a non-finite replicated statistic and the Poisson arrival cap. I take the flag and the refusals to be its whole effect.
bisect_quantile returns the midpoint once the CDF residual is at most 1e-12 and otherwise raises NotConverged after 200 bisections; it has no other effect. Refusal is its effect.

Equation 18.1.45 is a general weighting principle for a regression predictor with hyperparameters and prints no numerical example, so no printed value can be run on G6's posterior-predictive replication.
prior_shift only subtracts two posterior means, divides by the baseline sd and sets a boolean flag; it changes no posterior, label or draw. The flag is the 'note' effect.

checked() raises MLError for the faults the rule lists. When nothing is wrong it also computes the draws' mean, variance, sd and an empirical equal-tailed interval and returns them with the diagnostics; that summary is the sampler's descriptive output and changes no draw or label. I take refusal as its guarding effect, and that the summary changes nothing rests on my reading.

context_only.reason: Judged on the new wording: the register's clause now says the authors propose an R-hat on rank-normalized, folded draws (their section 4) and recommend using the sample only when it is below 1.01, with four or more chains as the default; that they recommend requiring the rank-normalized ESS to exceed 400; and that their software bounds the ESS estimate by S log10(S). I checked each against pages 4, 5 and 8 of the held paper (SHA-256 equal to the register's): it now says what the paper says, with the recommending tone and the modified R-hat, so the earlier tone and R-hat objections are gone and clause_fair would be true for what the clause states. It stays 'by context only' because the rule names more than the clause carries: splitting, the pooled ranks transform, folding, and the bulk and tail ESS definitions (sections 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.3), and a 400 line for tail-ESS, which the running text does not give; its support is the captions of the figures from page 13 on, which mark 400 as the recommended line on plots that include tail-ESS.

The clause states only the update and the beta mean and variance. The rule is the median and the equal-tail credible interval. I read section 8.6 (the interval from the lower and upper tail percentiles of the posterior, chosen for convenience over the shortest interval) and the percentile and median definitions in section 8.4; Table 8.2 prints the medians used in the cases.

The clause states the positive-uniform case only (shape equal to the total plus one, rate equal to the count, and Example 17's gamma(27,8)). The code also applies the update for a general gamma prior (add the total to the shape, the count to the rate), which the book gives a page later in the same chapter and adds that the same step also covers the flat positive prior; I read it. The clause omits it.

The register's own-words clause for page 8.9 gives the continued fraction 8.9.2 for the upper incomplete gamma function with its phase condition, and says outright that the series 8.7.1 for the lower function is on a page not held. I confirmed 8.9.2 against the page's TeX, term by term as far as the page prints it. The rule also names the power series for the lower function, which I could not read in the held bytes; I rely on its being the standard series and on the numerical agreement with mpmath.

The clause states the general Metropolis-Hastings ratio, the accept-if-at-least-one and compare-with-a-uniform steps of Algorithm 27.3, and the acceptance function of equation 27.4.7. The rule is the symmetric random-walk case, which the source reaches in the next paragraphs (a Gaussian proposal with equal forward and reverse densities makes the ratio p*(x')/p*(x), equations 27.4.11-27.4.12). The clause does not state that reduction; I read it.

The clause states the update and the beta mean and variance (the mean and variance formulas numbered 8.3 and, separately, 8.5). It says nothing of a mode or a standard deviation, and nothing of gamma or normal posteriors. I read the book's summary section: it gives the beta mode, defines the standard deviation as the root of the variance, and Table 8.2 prints the means and spreads used in the cases. The gamma mean, mode and spread are in chapter 10 and the normal ones in chapter 11, outside this entry.

not_checked: Issuer state qualified-draft: these checks were frozen after the code they check existed (a retrofit), so by the issuer's freeze rule they can reach qualified-draft at most. A named gap holds it at qualified-draft at most: the independent reader attested that a clause supports its rule only by its context (read by context only: convergence, credible_interval, gamma, gamma_cdf, mh, moments). A second route and invariants check these rules, and no value their source prints, by the independent reader's attestation (property-checked, no printed value: beta_cdf, convergence, evidence, gamma_cdf, mh, prediction).

Each printed case quotes its source with its inputs and values in one passage: beta from Bolstad Example 28 (Archie's posterior), gamma from Example 17 (Aretha's), normal from Example 29 (Andrea's posterior mean, through her prior's standard deviation and the sample mean; its printed standard deviation is lost to the conversion) and barber_example from Barber 9.1.31. Bolstad's Example 14 and 20 posteriors and Table 10.2's moments are printed away from their data, so they stay as known cases the case author transcribed (printed: false), not machine-quoted ones.

evidence is property-checked: Barber Example 12.2 prints the fair-coin evidences 0.0079 and 9.4 x 10^-21, but states their Beta(50,50) prior some 3,300 characters before them in the held file, beyond one quote, so no printed value can be quoted with its inputs; both stay as transcribed known cases. Evidence cases and generated inputs cover the beta-binomial model only; gamma-Poisson and normal evidence and Bayes factors remain outside this certificate. The posterior's moments and its median and equal-tailed interval are their own rules, moments (on exact.summary) and credible_interval (on exact.quantile): Bolstad Table 8.2's printed means, standard deviations and medians, and transcribed values of the second route for the gamma and normal posteriors and the interval's ends. evidence is checked on its beta-binomial form only.

Property-checked, because their sources print no value G6's functions can be run on: beta_cdf and gamma_cdf (DLMF 8.17 and 8.9, held as page bytes, state the functions, their fractions and their identities, not values; the series, the continued fractions and the switch between them are compared with SciPy on generated and boundary inputs; Barber's printed 0.9673 checks beta_cdf's function under barber_example), mh (Barber prints the algorithm, not a run: draws are compared with an independently written route using the same seeded standard-library random stream), convergence (the paper, held as PDF bytes, states the thresholds and the S log10(S) bound; no computed R-hat or ESS is compared with a printed value: rank and folded R-hat and bulk and tail ESS are compared with an independent route; lag autocovariances use the 1/N normalisation, which equation 10 does not fix; tail ESS above 400 is G6's stricter extension) and prediction (the normal posterior mixture only, not beta-binomial or gamma-Poisson replication, alternate statistics or calibration). Their known cases are identities and the case author's arithmetic, none printed by the source.

Each guard fires at its threshold, holds just inside it and fires on its recall set; G6's removal of it breaks its firing case, and a seeded change of its threshold or of a comparison at it is caught. What else its code does rests on the independent reader's word (effect_only). Their thresholds are G6's own. numerics checks the bisection bound of g6.core.special only (MAX_BISECTIONS); the 10,000-term bound of the series and fractions and the 128 bracket doublings are not reached by any case. bounds checks the observations' limits, not the typed input's ranges (the caller rule inputs). prior_shift checks the shift rule G6's prior-sensitivity reply applies (exact.prior_shift), not the reply's card.

PyMC's execute/child_main path requires an action-gated compiler and starts a further process; the certificate sandbox forbids further processes. PyMC sampling, divergences as PyMC reports them and optional-library compilation are not checked here.

Public request validation, dataset adaptation, large workloads, deadline enforcement, all quantile tails and accuracy over the entire continuous parameter space are not established by these finite cases.

register.clause: Barber, sections 9.1.3-9.1.4 (equations 9.1.24-9.1.26 and 9.1.28-9.1.31): for a coin whose probability of heads is theta, a Beta(alpha, beta) prior with N_H heads and N_T tails observed gives the posterior Beta(alpha + N_H, beta + N_T); prior and posterior share the Beta form, so Beta priors are conjugate for binomial data. The posterior probability that theta is below 0.5 is then I_0.5(alpha + N_H, beta + N_T), I_x(a, b) denoting the regularised incomplete Beta function; with a flat prior (alpha = beta = 1), 2 heads and 8 tails give I_0.5(N_H + 1, N_T + 1) = 0.9673.

register.clause: Barber, section 12.2.2 (equations (12.2.5) to (12.2.7), pp. 267-268, and Example 12.2): for a coin whose probability of heads is theta, with a Beta(a, b) prior (chosen for its conjugacy with the binomial), the likelihood of the fair-coin model given data D of N_H heads and N_T tails is p(D | M_fair) = the integral over theta of p(theta) theta^N_H (1 - theta)^N_T, which equals B(N_H + a, N_T + b) / B(a, b), B being the Beta function. The fair coin's prior is Beta(50, 50); Example 12.2 applies this to 5 heads and 2 tails, and to 50 heads and 20 tails.
register.derivation: G6 integrates the normalised prior times likelihood. Conjugate log normaliser ratios retain binomial coefficients, Poisson factorials and normal constants. Bayes factor is their ratio on identical observations.

register.clause: Barber, section 27.4.2 (equation 27.4.7, p. 547) and Algorithm 27.3, Metropolis-Hastings sampling (steps 4-10, p. 548): at step l a candidate x_cand is proposed from q~(x' | x_(l-1)), and the ratio a = q~(x_(l-1) | x_cand) p(x_cand) / (q~(x_cand | x_(l-1)) p(x_(l-1))) is formed. When a is 1 or more the candidate becomes x_l; otherwise u is drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1] and the candidate becomes x_l if u < a, while if not x_l stays equal to x_(l-1). This accepts with probability min(1, a), the acceptance function of equation 27.4.7, which is unchanged when p is replaced by an unnormalised p*.

register.clause: Barber, section 18.1.6, Prediction and model averaging, equation (18.1.45): when a prior is placed on the hyperparameters Gamma in addition to the weights w, the mean prediction at x averages f(x; w) over the joint posterior of w and Gamma given the data D: f-bar(x) = the double integral of f(x; w) p(w, Gamma | D) dw dGamma, which equals the integral over Gamma of [the integral of f(x; w) p(w | Gamma, D) dw] p(Gamma | D) dGamma. The inner integral is the predictor's mean at a fixed Gamma, so the outer integral weights each such mean by Gamma's posterior probability.

register.clause: Bolstad, chapter 8, Example 14 and the chapter's Main Points (pp. 147-155), with equations 8.3 and 8.5: for a binomial proportion, a beta(a, b) prior combined with y successes in n trials gives a beta posterior with parameters a' = a + y and b' = b + n - y; in words, the successes are added to a and the failures to b. Equation 8.3 gives its mean, a' / (a' + b'), and equation 8.5 its variance, a'b' / ((a' + b')^2 (a' + b' + 1)). The printed values checked are from Table 8.2 (p. 152) and from chapter 16, Example 28.

register.clause: Bolstad, chapter 10 (Positive uniform prior density, pp. 184-185; Example 17, pp. 187-190; Table 10.2): for n independent Poisson(mu) counts y_1, ..., y_n, the likelihood, as a function of mu, is shaped like a gamma density whose shape is one more than the total of the counts and whose rate is n. The positive uniform prior (g(mu) = 1 for every mu > 0) is improper, yet the posterior it gives is proper and has that same shape: gamma with shape (sum of y) + 1 and rate n. Under this prior, Example 17's eight weekly counts give gamma(27, 8).
register.derivation: Positive-uniform prior is explicit, accepted only with nonempty data; no marginal likelihood. Chase is not used.

register.clause: Bolstad, chapter 11 (equations 11.5-11.6, p. 209; Example 20, pp. 210-213; Known Variance, p. 212): for n independent observations from a normal(mu, sigma^2) distribution whose variance sigma^2 is known, the sample mean has a normal distribution of mean mu and variance sigma^2 / n. With a normal(m, s^2) prior (or a flat prior), mu then has the posterior normal(m', (s')^2), updated as follows: a precision is one over a variance; the posterior's precision is the prior's precision plus the sample mean's precision, n / sigma^2; and m', the posterior mean, averages m and the sample mean, each weighted by its precision's share of the posterior precision.

register.clause: Vehtari et al. (2021), section 2, p. 4: the authors propose an R-hat computed on rank-normalized, folded draws (their section 4) and recommend using the sample only when it is below 1.01, with four or more chains as the default. Section 2, p. 5: they recommend requiring the rank-normalized effective sample size (ESS) to exceed 400. Section 3.2, p. 8: the authors' software bounds the ESS estimate above by S log10(S), for S draws.
register.derivation: Source notes require R-hat <1.01. Split first; average pooled ranks for ties; z=Phi^-1((r-3/8)/(S+1/4)); fold about pooled median; maximum of rank and folded R-hat; tail ESS minimum at 5% and 95%. ESS uses within and between chain variance; each chain's autocorrelation weighted by its variance s2_m (equation 10: with divisor-N autocovariances, acov_t N/(N-1)); Geyer's initial positive monotone paired sums, the first pair always kept (equations 12-13); and the average of the sums truncated at the usual odd lag and at the next even lag, bounded by S log10(S) (p. 8). Tail ESS shares bulk ESS's 400: Figure 5 (p. 13) marks 400 as the recommended level on its plot of bulk and tail ESS. The hand-computed tests are G6 algebra applying equations 1-4 and 10-13, not examples printed in the paper.
register.issuing_body: Bayesian Analysis; Aki Vehtari, Andrew Gelman, Daniel Simpson, Bob Carpenter, Paul-Christian Burkner

register.section: Section 2, pp. 4-5 (four chains, R-hat below 1.01, rank-normalized ESS above 400); 3.1-3.2, pp. 5-8 (split R-hat; ESS, equations 10-13, the next-even-lag average and the S log10(S) bound); 4.1-4.3, pp. 9-10; Figure 5 caption, p. 13 (400 on bulk and tail ESS)
register.title: Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC

review.binding: SSH signature over the certificate's content digest (the record without its history positions), namespace g6-certificate; verified when given, never required to list

barber_example.rule: flat prior, two heads and eight tails

beta.rule: conjugate beta update: a' = a + the successes, b' = b + the failures

beta_cdf.rule: regularised beta CDF, symmetry and continued fraction (at most 10,000 terms to a relative tolerance of 2e-14, with a Lentz nonzero floor of 1e-300; refused when it does not converge)

bounds.rule: 1 to 20,000 observations, each a finite number of magnitude at most 1,000,000 and, for a count model, an integer count in the model's support whose total is at most 1,000,000; anything else is refused, as are neither or both of observations and a dataset, and a dataset row with an undeclared column or text beyond the family's limits

convergence.rule: split, ranks, folding, bulk and tail ESS; R-hat <1.01 and ESS >400

credible_interval.rule: the posterior's median and equal-tailed credible interval, from its quantiles

evidence.rule: marginal likelihood from normalised prior and likelihood, in its beta-binomial form (the gamma-Poisson and normal forms are not checked here)

gamma.rule: gamma shape-rate update and explicit positive-uniform prior

gamma_cdf.rule: regularised gamma series and continued fraction (at most 10,000 terms to a relative tolerance of 2e-14; refused when it does not converge)

inputs.rule: model, prior, noise, counts, credible mass and alternative priors, within the typed input's ranges (positive parameters .01 to 10,000; means within 1,000,000 of zero; binomial trials at most 10,000; at most 10 alternatives; mass .5 to .999; seed 0 to 2**32-1; 8 to 4,000 draws, 2 to 8 chains (default 4), 0 to 4,000 warmup; a proposal sd multiplier 1e-12 to 100 (default 2.4); at most 120 seconds (default 30); 50 to 1,000 predictive replicates and at most 2 million replicated observations and Poisson arrivals; dataset columns limited to the declared target and features, text to 10,000 characters a cell and 5,000,000 in all, checked before extraction or hashing; the PyMC child within the family's 1,536 MB and 32 MB output caps), refused beyond them

misfit.rule: warn if the observed statistic lies outside the stated predictive interval (a G6 warning; no calibrated hypothesis test or assurance of fit); refused instead for an unregistered statistic, more than 2,000,000 replicated observations, a variance of fewer than two observations or a non-finite observed statistic

moments.rule: the posterior's mean, variance, standard deviation and mode, for the beta, gamma and normal posteriors

normal.rule: normal precision update with separately known likelihood noise

numerics.rule: a quantile is the root of its CDF found by at most 200 bisections to a residual of 1e-12 in CDF units (where the density is small the quantile itself can be further off); when they do not reach it the calculation is refused, never answered approximately (a gamma quantile's bracket is doubled at most 127 times)

prior_shift.rule: warn if an alternative prior moves the posterior mean more than one baseline posterior sd (a G6 descriptive warning; a small shift is not evidence a prior is justified)

sampler_metadata.rule: finite in-support draws, complete chains with no exact duplicates, and integer zero PyMC divergences, or the sample is refused; it is refused too when R-hat is not below 1.01 or the bulk or tail ESS is not above 400 (rule convergence's thresholds)
